# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the transaction enrichment logic.

### Enrichment pipeline (per bank branch of `Controller.py`, e.g. HDFC at `:163-186`)

```
AppUtil.clean_input_df                      → strip description, numeric amount/balance
categorize_<Bank>_transactions(...)         → transactionCategory, transactionSubcategory, merchantType, partyName, party2
  (if CREDIT_CARD) card_clean_names → card_purpose
purpose(transactions, accountType)          → transactionSubcategory + category overrides + merchantType
clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)→ canonical partyName (merchant dictionary) + party2 + a few sub-cat fixes
internal_payment(...)                       → INTERNAL_PAYMENT via fuzzy match with accountHolder
salary_detection(...)     (SAVING only)     → SALARY / REIMBURSEMENT via Levenshtein clustering
pfm_categorization + simple_description     (only if isPFMEnabled)
```

Every stage uses the same idiom: a list of `[boolean-Series condition, choice]` pairs fed to `np.select(...)` — **first matching row wins**, so ordering inside these lists is the de-facto rule priority.

def mk(rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for c in ["remark"]:
        if c not in df:
            df[c] = ""
    if "balanceAfterTransaction" not in df:
        df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = 1000.0
    return df


def show(title, out):
    print("=" * 70)
    print(title)
    print(out[["description", "remark", "type", "amount"] + COLS].to_string())


# ---- 1. HDFC: all-numeric remark on a credit should be CHEQUE_DEPOSIT

    {"description": "MR SOMEBODY", "remark": "000000000112345", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 5000.0},
])
show("1. HDFC cheque deposit via 15-char numeric remark (expect CHEQUE_DEPOSIT)",
     categorize_HDFC_transactions(df, "SAVING"))

    {"description": "TRFR TO:RAVI KUMAR", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1500.0},
    {"description": "TRFR FROM:PRIYA SHARMA", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 1500.0},
])

     categorize_ICICI_transactions(df, "SAVING"))

])

     categorize_ICICI_transactions(df, "SAVING"))

All five reported issues are fixed with five one-token corrections in two files. Summary:

## Root causes

**HDFC (`BankScripts/HDFC.py`)**

1. **Cheque deposit → generic transfer** (`:100`) — the rule gated on `remark.str.len().eq(15)` but the regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 characters, so the condition was unsatisfiable and every such credit fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Fixed to `^[0]{10}[0-9]{5}` (consumes exactly the 15-char gate; the 16-char remark rules at `:214-215` are untouched).

2. **Salary sub-tag lost on bare-numeric narrations** (`:124`) — compared `accountType=="SAVINGS"`; the pipeline only ever passes `"SAVING"` (Controller, `Purpose.py`, `InternalPayment.py`), so the rule never fired. Fixed to `"SAVING"`.

3. **Reversal recorded as bounce** (`:98`) — the paired-row REVERSAL rule compared `description.eq(description.shift(2))` while its debit sits one row above, so the offsetting credit skipped it and matched the next rule (`AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`, `:99`). Fixed to `shift(1)`, matching the identical rule in `ICICI.py:49` and `Saraswat.py:20`.

**ICICI (`BankScripts/ICICI.py`)**

4. **Counterparty empty or wrong on direction-word narrations** (`:159`) — `py_extract(pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 1, i.e. the direction word itself. `"To"` was then scrubbed to empty by the `^[A-Z]{1,2}$` cleanup at `:233`, while `"From"` survived as the payee. Fixed to `index=1` (the name group), matching `DCB.py:80-81` and `ICICI.py:168`.

5. **Wrong payee on 4-field slash references** (`:147`) — `BIL/INFT/<ref>/<payee>` used `sep_by_(2,3)`, lifting the numeric reference (then wiped by the `[0-9]{6,}` cleanup at `:233`) instead of the trailing name. Fixed to `sep_by_(3,4)`, consistent with the 5-field variants at `:148`/`:154`.

## Verification

Built a full-pipeline harness (`categorize_* → purpose → clean_names → internal_payment → salary_detection → pfm_categorization → simple_description`) over 124 rows/bank-account-type combos covering UPI, IMPS, NEFT/RTGS, POS, ATM, NACH/ACH, cheque, charges, reversal and refund paths, plus the edge rows from the thread, and diffed output before vs. after the change:

- 13 changed cells, all on the exact rows described in the thread (`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` restored, `SALARY` sub-tag restored, `REVERSAL` instead of `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`, `Ravi Kumar`/`Priya Sharma`/`Acme Traders` payees restored).
- Everything else byte-identical, including nearby rules that could have been over-captured: 16-digit remark rows (`:214-215`), the 9-leading-zero remark, the 7-digit narration, non-transfer offsetting pairs (still `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`), the 5-field `BIL/INFT` variant, and ICICI IMPS reversal pairs.
